improved: Campaign forest maps render up to twice as fast on the GPU, and every map a little faster, with the same picture

added: Unit movement rebuilt in the manner of StarCraft II: your own units part for each other, squeeze through chokes and close round their targets, while enemies and units fighting or holding position still block
Heroes stand out: a golden burst when they gain a level, a level badge and a glowing card while a skill point waits, and a soft pool of their player's colour
An army button and key (F1), groups of buildings that share their training and research, and grid hotkeys for every command card cell
Windowed, borderless and exclusive fullscreen display modes, and a Voice volume setting
Reset campaign, to play a campaign again from the start
improved: Four unit body sizes, with every model scaled to the space it takes
Substance Wells pump faster: 10 Substance every 3 seconds
Queued units take supply only once they start training, and Reaver Queens and Juggernauts are no longer limited to one
Buildings sit firmly on the ground, with a soft shadow at their base
The third ant mission's beetles no longer rebuild what you destroy
fixed: Neutral camps and computer players fight back together, ranged attackers included
Melee units no longer jam or vibrate behind allies already fighting
The camera reaches the edges and corners of the map, and on macOS exclusive fullscreen keeps hot corners away
Animation, sleeping-creature and ramp fixes

Skirmish with two races, the ants and the beetles, each with three heroes
improved: A new block map editor: shape maps in blocks with generated cliffs, ramps and water, symmetry tools, a minimap, pathing and split views, and StarCraft II map import
Campaign support: linear campaigns with story pages, chapter cards and loading screens, heroes carried between missions, tech unlocked mission by mission, and computer allies and enemies
In-mission cinematics: letterboxed scenes, camera shots that find whoever is speaking, and live speaker portraits
Play with AI: a mission can play itself at up to 8× speed, slowing to normal speed for its cutscenes
A new forest biome, a full lighting pass, natural shores and flowing rivers, and an enchanted forest weather
Neutral map features: breakable crates and rubble, healing springs and a travelling merchant
Player 1 is always blue, a quieter objective list, a plump gold loot sack for dropped items, and a new main menu
fixed: Many fixes to pathfinding, tunnels and computer players

added: Beetles now have a steel, brass and violet-magic HUD frame and resource ribbon; Ants keep their woodland interface.
Ants travel underground: units ordered far away walk to their nearest mound and come up at the mound nearest their destination, a few at a time per mound

The ant army is complete: Raiders hatch in pairs and frenzy together, Needlers fire chitin needles, Bursters run in and burst, Majors guard and plug, Honeypots lob nectar, Heralds lay scent trails and sound the alarm, Gardeners grow healing fungus, Alates fly ahead and found new mounds, Bullet Ants sting, and the Reaver Queen devours

Three ant heroes with four abilities each: the Queen (Found Colony raises a Brood Mound where she points, Royal Jelly heals and strengthens an ally, One Body shares the colony's wounds, and the Exodus ultimate sinks her army underground and brings it up beside any ally), the Royal Alchemist (Volatile Draught, Transfusion, Crystallise, and the Overdose ultimate) and the General (Mandible Charge, Mark Prey, War Column, and the Bivouac ultimate that locks the army into a living fortress)
Ant research at the Chitin Works, the Fungus Garden and the Brood Mound, and the Venom Spire tower upgrade
improved: A building works on one thing at a time: research waits for the units queued before it, and units for the research, as in Warcraft III. Its queue panel shows training, research and revivals in the order you queued them.

Ant buildings are rebuilt as sculpted sand-clay spire cathedrals with royal-blue drapes and glowing blossoms; each one animates while it works (swaying banners, opening mandibles, a dipping blade, a breathing crown)
The beetle Bombard is about a third smaller and the Juggernaut half its former size, so they no longer dwarf the army

Ant units have new models and portraits that read from above: the Worker, a stocky biting Raider, the needle-firing Needler, the armoured Major, a swollen amber Honeypot, the winged Alate, the Bullet Ant and the General, each animated as it walks, fights, casts and dies
The ants' Herald and Gardener have new six-legged models that walk on all six legs, and the Royal Alchemist hero has its model
Computer ant players found mounds near the front and send their armies through the tunnels
Every ant spell has its own visible cast and landing: casters glow and draw a sigil as they wind up, and hero spells raise pillars of light, so you can see who cast what
Ant heroes and the Major stand larger on the field, and every ant weapon lands with its own hit effect

Every beetle spell has its own look and a visible cast: casters wind up over a turning brass gear or arc glyph, Overload drains mana into an orb that bursts, Unbottled is a turning violet vortex, the Bolt Turret assembles from swirling plates, shields are hexagon domes and the Juggernaut's barrage walks across the ground

The Hornbreaker has his own spell effects: Horn Rush throws up a wall of dust behind him and bursts the earth where he lands, Steadfast lays a brass shield sigil under his allies, and Colossus ignites his furnace, blasts steam from his vents and leaves burning footprints
Beetle heroes stand larger on the field, as tall as the ant heroes

Computer opponents play with personalities: a rusher attacks early with its first units and skips the creeps, an expander takes a second base early and out-produces you, a technologist races up the tiers for its strongest units, and the rest play a steady all-round game. Each computer player picks one per match
Computer heroes save mana for their ultimates, so Unbottled, Overdose, Exodus and the other ultimates now appear in matches against the computer

Balance from hundreds of computer matches: Raider pairs cost 150 amber (was 160) with 185 health (was 170) and 8 damage (was 7); the General has 900 health, 44 damage and 4 armor, and War Column gives 10/15/20%; Lock Shields gives 4 armor and 30% less piercing damage (7 and 45% with Interlocking Shields); Overclock is 30/45/60%; Forgefall deals 200/300; Horn Rush recharges in 14 seconds instead of 10

Every icon is repainted to read at a glance: one clear subject per icon, near-invisible backgrounds, passives at full brightness with a pulse mark, gold marks for research levels, and upgrades that visibly improve the same object
A hero's Abilities sit in the eighth command slot with a count of unspent skill points, instead of a "New spell available" banner that showed even with no points to spend

Forgefall is rebuilt with new effect tools: a red-hot anvil falls trailing fire and smoke that hang in the air, lands, and sends a blast wave of fire racing out over the ground that cools into drifting ash
Spell effects fade softly where they meet the ground, units and buildings instead of cutting into them
Every ranged attack now leaves a trail: arrows and thorns a faint wake, nectar and venom glowing comet tails with falling drops, beetle bolts a violet streak, and siege shells arcs of fire and smoke
Ranged forest creatures fire their own magic: willow lights, dew bolts, bloom and spore shots in their own colours, each bursting where it lands
Beetle lightning forks and branches: Arc Lash, Arc Surge, Overload, the Unbottled storm and the beetles' arc weapons crackle with jagged, forking bolts
Pressure Mains is researched at the Brood Den, the network building it upgrades, instead of the Great Bastion
fixed: Computer Shieldbearers no longer lock their shields from afar and stand rooted behind their own army
releases.title: The ant colony

added: 0.4 is the first milestone since the native rebuild: the beetles join the ants as a second complete, playable race; the forest runs on a new economy of amber and Substance, pumped from wells on contested deposits; and Echo Isles shows the game's new autumn forest look.

The road to 0.4, the 0.3 series in one place: the native game for Apple Silicon Macs (0.3.0), Warcraft-style lobbies and teaming up against the computer (0.3.2), smooth movement (0.3.4), a smarter computer opponent and your own maps (0.3.5), the game's own editor with twelve classic Warcraft III battlefields and Amberleaf Crossing (0.3.6), and replays with in-game feedback (0.3.7).
A look-dev showcase map, Look-dev: Fall, previews the new forest-floor look: giant trunks, leaf litter, mushrooms, a shallow ford, a deep pool and glowing amber
Look-dev: Fall has a canopy: giant trees rise into it in the third-person view, light falls through it in beams with dust and drifting leaves, and the distant forest goes soft with depth of field.

Beetles build on a substance network: their halls power the ground around them and Brood Dens extend it in a chain. War Lodges, Shell Forges, Hornwatches and Ancestor Shrines must be placed inside it and stop working while cut off; placing one shows the network on the ground, and a dark building shows a struck-bolt badge.

Substance Wells: build one on top of a Substance Deposit, as a refinery sits on its geyser, and it pumps Substance into your stock by itself, about 120 a minute, while it stands; no workers needed. The deposit never runs dry and stands again when its well falls.

The beetles are a complete race: Bastion tiers up to the Elder Bastion, War Lodge, Shell Forge, Alembic, Engine Yard, Hornwatch and Arc Tower, Ancestor Shrine; Tinkers, Shieldbearers, Bolters, Breachers, Arcwrights, Menders, Wardens, Bombards, Steamwings and the one-at-a-time Juggernaut, with tiered forge research and lodge, alembic and yard upgrades.

Two new beetle heroes beside the Hornbreaker: the Forgemaster deploys Bolt Turrets, Overclocks allies, keeps a Field Forge burning and calls down Forgefall, a crucible that slams into a warning circle and leaves a molten pool; the Coilkeeper lashes chains of violet lightning, Overloads enemy mana, Recharges allies and, once, goes Unbottled into a storm that drags enemies in and lifts them off the ground.

Wardens raise a field barrier that stops enemy arrows and bolts from the front and makes shells burst against it; Shieldbearers lock shields into an armoured wall; Arcwright arcs and the Arc Tower jump between enemies; Bombards cannot fire at anything close.
Beetle weapons have muzzle flashes, steam, violet tracers and sparks on every shot, and drill sparks and impact dust in melee.
Skirmish lets you pick each player's colour, as the multiplayer lobby does
Amber your workers bring in and Substance your wells pump rise as floating numbers where they arrive. Turn them off under Settings, Gameplay.
improved: Look-dev: Fall now has a painted forest floor around its clearing, sun glints on its shallow ford, and amber that sits in a crater.
The beetles' Shell Forge has a new model that comes alive while it researches: the furnace glows, the chimneys smoke and the hammer strikes the anvil in a shower of sparks; at rest it stands still.
The Shell Forge is larger, sized against the main hall like a Warcraft III Blacksmith, fills its footprint and no longer sits on a patch of dirt.
The second resource, Root, is now called Substance (a working name).
Every icon in one hand-painted style: new portraits, ability and research icons for the beetles, the ants, neutral creatures and items redrawn to match, and new command, armour and resource icons.

Trees are no longer a resource: wood is gone from every cost. Basic buildings and units cost a little more amber, and advancing your hall and the tier-2 roster costs Substance instead. Tree walls still block the way.
Echo Isles has two Substance Deposits between the bases to fight over, and every other skirmish map has one near each start.
Computer players build Substance Wells, spend Substance, and attack an enemy's well when they have none of their own.
Beetle Substance Wells also power the ground around them, so beetles can build out by a well they hold; the well itself needs no power and goes wherever its deposit is.
Units can show their own effects: muzzle blasts, footstep dust and exhaust follow their animations, and machines' glowing parts light up while they move, fight or cast.
Buildings and resource deposits can glow and mist at rest, and work visibly while they produce.
The beetles' Substance Well and the Substance Deposit have their own models: the well fills the deposit exactly, seeps at rest, and pumps and arcs while it works.

The computer opponent keeps its Substance Wells defended, raises towers over its workers when raided, places powered buildings inside its network before extending it, and no longer stalls on research or upgrades it cannot start yet.
Computer opponents build a new hall at the next amber field before theirs runs dry, clearing the creeps that guard it, and defend their outlying halls
Computer opponents start with a varied hero instead of always the first one
The Forgemaster's Bolt Turret and the Arc Tower have their own models: a horned brass repeater on a tripod and a towering substance coil that lights up when it fires
Beetle Wardens carry a glowing violet barrier pane, so they stand out in an army at a glance

Every beetle ability and research now has its own icon: Static Field, Bulwark Pulse, Broadside, Furnace Plating, Flak Beam, Patch Up and Armor Breaker are new, and Weapon Edges, Bolt Calibre, Plating and Riveted Hulls show one icon per level instead of borrowed ant art.

Beetle weapons and spells are crisp and readable: hot violet tracers and muzzle flashes on every volley, sparks that streak, star-bright impacts, shock rings and glass shards instead of soft white blobs
Forgefall drops a real iron crucible out of the canopy, trailing fire, onto a pool of molten metal
The Hornwatch turns its turret to face its target, and the Hornwatch and Arc Tower flash and discharge on every shot
Computer opponents search the map with their whole army for the last enemy buildings, so a won match ends
Computer opponents add production when goods pile up, learn every hero ability before raising ranks, learn and cast ultimates first, and keep buffs and shields for fights

Beetles build up more slowly but hit harder: their troops and machines train longer and the Great and Elder Bastion, Alembic and Engine Yard cost more, while their troops are sturdier and deal more damage, so beetles hold their own against ants.
Echo Isles is now an autumn forest map: dark leaf-strewn woods, pine needles and moss on the open ground, calm shallows and dark pools
Levelled research shows one level at a time: once Plating I is queued, its button turns into Plating II, waiting for the first to finish
fixed: Sparks and shrapnel from spells and weapons fall instead of flying up, and steam rises
The Brood Den pressurises while it powers the network, and the Juggernaut crashes down in a burst of sparks and dust when destroyed
Computer opponents no longer favour one side of a map when they look for building sites
Matches between computer opponents no longer stall when both run out of amber
Dark forest edges are now solid: units can no longer walk or build where the ground looks impassable
Beetle units stand on the ground instead of floating above it
Units stay over their selection circle: walking, running and carrying no longer pull the model ahead of where the unit really is
A Substance deposit stays visible while its Well is being built: the scaffold rises around it and the finished Well takes its place
A selected building that can both train and research, such as the Bastion, again shows its training queue and progress
Damaged buildings of every race visibly burn from the first tenth of lost health, with flames that read at game zoom on the large beetle buildings
knownIssues: The beetles and the ants are not balanced against each other yet: in computer matches the beetles win fewer than half their games. A balance pass follows.
releases.title: The beetles

added: Submit feedback from the main menu or the game menu: describe a bug, idea or balance problem and it is sent with a screenshot of what you were looking at; reports written offline are sent later.

Replays: every match is recorded. Save it from the result screen, or find your latest match as Last match, and watch it from Skirmish → Replays with a timeline, speeds, any player's vision and statistics.
Feedback sent from a match includes its replay and a save of that moment.
fixed: Watching a match after playing one no longer shows the previous match's fog of war.
releases.title: Replays and feedback

added: Under the Canopy's own editor, opened from the main menu when the game runs from its repository (for now the team's tool): forms for every unit, building, item, ability, effect and race with one undo history and Test in game; a Warcraft III-style map editor that also imports Warcraft III melee maps; an asset editor; an ability Stage that casts spells on test targets with the real simulation; and an MCP server so agents can edit too.

Amberleaf Crossing, a new 1v1 map: mains on high ground in opposite corners, a river winding through a lake with a contested island, high-ground expansions in the far corners and fifteen creep camps that grow harder away from your base.

Twelve classic Warcraft III melee maps for 2 to 8 players: Terenas Stand, Amazonia, Northern Isles, Last Refuge, Concealed Hill, Twisted Meadows, Lost Temple, Hillsbrad Creek, Gnoll Wood, Silverpine Forest, Bloodstone Mesa and Twilight Ruins, in the game's own ground, trees and creeps.
Maps can frame their playable area with a border of forest, cliffs and water that nobody enters; the camera and minimap stay on the playable area.
improved: Maps with large forests run faster.
Neutral creeps grow with their strength, as in Warcraft III: the weakest are about a Warrior's size and the strongest tower over heroes.
fixed: A match no longer crashes when a unit that cannot move steers around others.

Computer players no longer get stuck in their base: armies no longer freeze when one unit can't get through, give up targets they can't reach, and units wedged against cliff edges beside ramps step free.
knownIssues: Artifacts dropped by creeps show a placeholder box on the ground until their models are made.
The Beetles' workers and two of their buildings show a placeholder box until their models are made.
releases.title: Classic battlefields and an editor

added: Your own maps appear in Skirmish: put a map package (a .utcm folder) into the maps folder in the game's user folder.
improved: The computer opponent fields its whole army roster — casters, Queensguard, Winglancers and more, not just Warriors, Archers and Hunters — and chooses what to train from what its buildings offer and what its enemy fields; AI duels now end decisively instead of stalling for an hour.
knownIssues: Games saved in 0.3.4 or earlier can't be loaded: the game's content has a new structure.
releases.title: A smarter enemy and your own maps

added: An idle worker button above the minimap shows how many workers have nothing to do; click it to select the next one.
Alt-click the minimap to ping a spot for your team: a ring pulses there on their minimaps for four seconds.
A computer player says gg in the chat when its colony is defeated.
improved: A fallen hero keeps their portrait in the top left, greyed out, and shows the seconds left while they are being revived.

Unit movement is much smoother, in the spirit of StarCraft II: units set off and turn at once, ease around each other, slide past instead of stopping dead, push idle allies out of the way, stream through chokepoints and stop together around their destination instead of fighting for the spot.

The computer opponent fights with its whole army: wounded units no longer pile up idle in its base, it gathers out of its workers' way, waits for a stronger army before attacking and sends reinforcements in groups.
fixed: Fallen heroes can be revived again: the Sanctuary and Ancestor Shrine offer Revive for each fallen hero.
Right-clicking the minimap orders the selection there without the camera jumping to that spot.
Items on the ground are much easier to pick up: they are picked where they are drawn, with the same generous target as units, including items lying in water.
Workers carry their load to the drop-off nearest the mine or tree they work, so a new Hall by the amber is used straight away instead of the old one across the map.
Pressing Enter in a match opens the chat again instead of restarting the match.
releases.title: Smooth movement

fixed: The game no longer eats all memory and freezes the Mac while its window is minimised, hidden or covered.
releases.title: No more runaway memory

added: A small graph button next to Menu opens the debug overlay (frame rate, timings and match tools), so it no longer needs F9.

Multiplayer lobbies work like Warcraft III: the host sets each seat to Open, Closed or Computer, and every seat picks its race, hero, team and colour. Play 2v2 with a friend against the computer, or lock seats to play a 4-player map with two.
improved: The lobby map shows each seat's chosen colour and hides starts nobody will play.
The multiplayer lobby list shows only lobbies you can join: started matches are hidden, and finished or abandoned ones disappear on their own.
fixed: Multiplayer matches can start with fewer players than the map has starts: unused starts stay empty instead of the match failing to load.
releases.title: Team up against the computer

added: With a worker selected, hovering a tree shows a ring around it, so you can tell trees can be clicked to gather wood.
Damaged buildings catch fire: flames and smoke grow as their health falls and die down when they are repaired.
Melee hits throw up a puff of dust along the swing.
improved: Damaged buildings show their health bars, as damaged units do.
Ant Warriors deal 14 damage instead of 9.
Buildings on sloping ground no longer float: the ground rises to meet them, in the same grass, earth or rock as around it.
fixed: Right-clicking a tree works anywhere on the tree, trunk or crown, instead of only exactly at its base.
Buildings can be placed on rolling hills: only cliffs, ramps and water block construction, so "Choose flatter ground" no longer refuses most of the map.
releases.title: Building on hills, burning buildings

added: Under the Canopy is rebuilt as a native game for Apple Silicon Macs. Skirmish, multiplayer, spectating, settings and key bindings work as in 0.2.
Graphics presets (Low, Medium, High, Ultra) are chosen for your Mac on first start and can be changed in Settings → Graphics.
A redesigned What's new screen shows every release, and the main menu checks for updates as before.
Skirmish setup lets you choose each player's team.
The result screen shows match statistics.
Optional construction, training and cast bars appear under the health bars of selected units and buildings.
improved: Large battles with hundreds of units run smoothly: the simulation is several times faster than in 0.2.
Right-clicking an allied unit with your army moves there instead of attacking it. Use Attack to force an attack.
Escape cancels the current mode first, then goes back, then opens the game menu.
On macOS, Cmd works like Ctrl for control groups.
The minimap shows the world as seen from above.
The day and night cycle follows match time: it stops while the game is paused, and a loaded save continues at the right hour.

Computer opponents play better: archers keep their distance from melee units, workers are assigned more sensibly, they no longer send units to resources they have not seen, and they judge spells by their full effect.
The third-person unit camera stays at the right distance and no longer passes through trees and buildings.
fixed: Workers that cannot reach a damaged building wait before trying again, instead of slowing the game by retrying constantly.
Finished multiplayer matches are reported to the server, so they no longer stay listed as playing in the lobby.
knownIssues: Saves from 0.2 versions cannot be loaded.
Everyone in a multiplayer match needs version 0.3.0; it cannot play with 0.2 versions.
The map editor is not included in this version.
Only Macs with Apple Silicon are supported for now.
Performance has not yet been measured on base M1 Macs. If matches stutter, choose the Low preset in Settings → Graphics.
Uproot's spell models look lighter than in 0.2.
releases.title: The native game

improved: Spell effects prepare their assets and shaders before matches, reuse a fixed light pool, and batch particles to reduce first-cast hitching and draw calls.
Crowded combat approaches reject blocked routes earlier, reducing long positioning spikes without changing route choices.

Long-distance movement now repairs collision-safe navigation corners before falling back to expensive grid searches, reducing army-order stalls. Navigation diagnostics also show why mesh routes fall back.
Units standing against terrain or buildings now use mesh routing across its tiny safety margin, avoiding unnecessary long grid searches while retaining full collision checks.

Combat units reuse terrain-valid attack positions across retries and skip duplicate clearance checks. Only nearby blocker changes invalidate those positions; moving units and reservations are still checked live.
Attack-position searches reuse a snapshot of nearby collision bodies, and wide collision queries skip empty map cells while preserving collision and query order.
Combat path planning reuses terrain clearance checks and skips empty reservation scans, reducing repeated work during battles.
Reduced expensive pathfinding fallbacks near shoreline and building corners while preserving exact destinations and collision checks.
Reduced repeated terrain-footprint checks and temporary allocations when combat units choose attack positions, without changing movement or collision rules.
knownIssues: Large battles can still produce simulation spikes; the 3 ms p99 non-render performance target is not yet met.
releases.title: Smoother combat and spell effects

improved: Updated the multiplayer server with current race and starting-hero selection support.
fixed: Native macOS models retain their natural material colors beneath player-color masks instead of rendering those surfaces black.
Fixed desktop multiplayer connection failures by using trusted HTTPS and secure WebSockets.
releases.title: Secure multiplayer connections

images.alt: Rootbreaker in Echo Isles, with all four hero skills in the first row.
images.caption: Rootbreaker in Echo Isles, with all four hero skills in the first row.

added: Release notes can include image galleries with captions and a larger keyboard-accessible viewer.
Match Debug now includes a terrain-following world grid shared with the map editor.
Choose your starting hero in skirmish and multiplayer setup. Ants can start with the Marshal or Rootbreaker; choices persist through saves and restarts.
Hall tiers now unlock distinct hero roster slots. Sanctuary recruitment and revival share one ordered queue, preserve fallen heroes, and support deterministic save/load.
Added Amberwake Basin as a competitive 1v1 playtest with four-node amber sites, opening timber, guarded expansions and editable forest scenery; route pacing is still being tuned.
Amberwake Frost joins Amberwake Basin as a paired two-player playtest, with matching terrain, resource positions and movement collision.
Amberwake Wilds adds a woodland showcase with giant oaks, ruined watches, hollow logs and living shore vegetation on the new two-player competitive layout.
Missions can define loading and selection artwork, chapter labels, briefings, and rotating loading tips in Mission & Lua; campaign loading uses a stylized progress bar.
The Ant Marshal now has four learnable abilities with original icons and editable effects: Faultline, Rally the Colony, Iron Carapace, and Crownfall.
Map preview images now show every player start with a colored marker and P1, P2, and subsequent player labels.
Choose Ants or Beetles in skirmish and multiplayer. Race-specific starting armies, building and unit rosters, hero choices, research, AI and campaign settings now share one configuration system.

Added the playable Beetle baseline with matching worker economics, Horn Guards, Stone Slingers with visible projectiles, colony buildings and Hornbreaker. His kit includes Horn Rush, stacking Overwhelm, Steadfast Aura and Colossus; Beetle models remain placeholders until their art is ready.
Spell authoring now supports terrain-aware caster charges and capped, source-specific stacking statuses with per-stack modifiers and primary-attack damage bonuses.
Added Echo Isles and Last Refuge 1v1 maps traced from classic Warcraft III layouts, with dense woodland, resource sites, neutral camps and labeled previews.
Added Warcraft ground texture source assets with preserved transition atlases, material channels, and preview images.
Added Warcraft map import for editable terrain, ground textures, trees, player starts, amber sites and difficulty-matched neutral camps.

Expanded the editor terrain palette to all ground definitions covered by the supplied Rebirth replacements, with missing texture channels supplied by the local Reforged installation and visual previews for each material.

Cliff-face terrain textures can be painted and erased independently of ground textures, with thumbnails, undo and editable Warcraft import coverage. Echo Isles and Turtle Rock now include their source cliff material.
Moving ground units leave fading water ripples and wakes, with bounded rendering for large groups and a relaxed walking cadence.
Maps can start explored under fog or fully hidden. Skirmishes default to explored and campaigns to hidden; unseen enemy activity remains concealed.

Silkwardens can now be trained at ant barracks, firing silk shots and automatically ensnaring enemies. Their animated model has a rigid casting net, a large silk spool, and team-colored leaf armor; snares root ground units and temporarily ground flyers.

Nectarists can now be trained at ant barracks. Their animated leaf-robed model carries a nectar jar and bowl, automatically heals wounded allies with traveling nectar, and can manually cleanse harmful effects. Healing and cleanse visuals remain editable in the Spell Editor.
Ant barracks can recruit Bannerets, whose Rallying Standard boosts nearby allies' damage. Includes an animated standard bearer, player-color leaves and banner, and editable rally effects.
Amber Adepts can now be trained at ant barracks, with an animated ring staff, readable team-colored leaf mantle, amber bolts, enemy-buff dispel and an autocast silence that lasts less time on heroes.
Queensguards join the ant barracks as larger elite protectors, with tower shields, protection auras and shield brace.
Winglancers join the ant barracks as flying ground-attack troops, with four-wing flight animations, readable team colors, and a place in the mixed-army combat preview.
Rootweavers join the ant barracks with automatic Root Bind and a persistent Briar Patch that slows and damages ground enemies.
Unit assets can declare a hero model class with a 10,000-triangle budget, including attachments; regular unit models retain the 5,000-triangle limit.
Rootbreaker's finished hero model includes broad team-color armor, ten animation clips and editable source assets, with overhead previews in every player color.
Spell Editor statuses can now taunt enemies temporarily, with immunity, dispels, and restoration of their previous orders.

Rootbreaker joins the ant hero roster with Crushing Presence, Skullcrack, Challenge Roar and Uproot, including animated roots, spell icons and combat effects. Choose him at match start or recruit him as a second hero after upgrading the Hall.

Terrain authoring is grid-first: paint levels, cliffs, banks, ramps and water regions with automatic straight, diagonal and corner connections, then refine individual cells or sculpt hills. Maps save the editable terrain directly; generators run only in the editor and Apply commits their results.
Shallow water supports walkable fords and submerged crossings, with terrain depth shared by rendering, navigation and AI; deep water blocks ground movement.

Thornblades join the ant army with oversized paired daggers, readable player-colored armor, alternating stabbing and slashing attacks, and an autocast rapid charge with editable trail and impact effects.
improved: Reduced unnecessary collision-index preparation during combat planning while preserving movement and combat behavior.
A zinc changelog timeline shows release history, with category icons and automatic desktop update availability on the main menu.
Reduced fog-of-war terrain calculations by retaining compact visibility footprints and skipping ray tests over proven-clear terrain. Visibility still updates at the same frequency.
Rebuilt the main menu with a dark woodland battlefield, carved charcoal controls, animated canopy light shafts and small fires, and a compact version label.
Units now handle nearby traffic with local detours and yielding instead of repeatedly recalculating routes across the map, reducing movement spikes in crowded matches.
Made menu light shafts brighter with drifting beams and dust, narrowed menu buttons, and enlarged and aligned fires with damaged buildings.
Shifted menu canopy rays away from the right trunk and added finer shafts through the left opening.
Extended menu fire smoke into taller drifting plumes and tripled the rising sparks.
Reduced nearby collision and visibility bookkeeping during unit movement while preserving movement and sight rules.
Added a forest-backed campaign selector with ant, beetle and bee crests, Play and Locked states, fading navigation, and a campaign-only dark backdrop.
Reduced simulation spikes from fallen heroes and AI building placement, and reused navigation connectivity when local obstacle edits leave routes connected the same way.
Reduced temporary simulation allocations and unnecessary AI harvesting searches while preserving combat and harvesting decisions.
Earned resources now belong to the player wallet and survive building destruction; cancellations refund directly even without a Hall.
Buildings now use a shared placement grid with exact footprints and snapped entrances; the editor shows building-cell dimensions and exposes a Grid toggle.
Unit sizes, movement speeds, weapon reach and starting formations now follow explicit competitive grid measurements; local movement recovery handles larger bodies.
Amber nodes now serve one miner at a time with waiting queues and no worker cap. Four-node sites target eight workers; trees hold fifty wood and fall only when depleted.

Competitive construction and training now use defined costs and timings. Foundations pause without a builder and support right-click resumption; cancellation refunds 75%. Colonies can rebuild a lost Hall while another building survives, without losing their wallet.
Hero revival now uses level-based prices and times, shows paid queue costs, preserves progress through save/load, and lets AI save for fallen veterans.
Player starts can face any cardinal direction, rotating the Hall and its complete formation together for mirrored map openings.
Amberwake Basin playtest now has two balanced 45-second approaches, larger construction shelves, and safer first-camp positions.
The standard RTS camera now frames the new building grid, showing base space and nearby approaches while keeping units readable.
Retired the old-scale project maps and updated editor and benchmark defaults to Amberwake; browser-saved maps remain recoverable.
Unreachable routes into enclosed bases are rejected with bounded checks, avoiding expensive full-map searches.
Computer opponents choose body-clear retreat and rally points and leave base service lanes for larger trainable units.

Amberwake Wilds now uses large forest masses to shape its routes, with living grass and undergrowth that fade from tree edges into open dirt. The forest-driven meadow recipe is available in the editor foliage list.
Map selection and multiplayer lobbies now display battlefield dimensions in the same building cells as the editor grid.
Amber sites now form staggered arcs with two close and two distant nodes. All three Amberwake maps retain mirrored resource layouts and clear worker return lanes.
Amber deposits now form compact, touching clusters with two near and two far nodes, while keeping starting workers and mining approaches clear.

Amber sites now centre five touching nodes beneath the Hall, with ten recommended miners. Health bars retain a consistent screen size and show a smooth red-to-green fill, 100-HP dividers and a separate mana row for casters.
Rebuilt The Amber Watch with a lantern-road woodland map, neutral camp detours, recruitable patrols, Lua cinematics, and a siege finale.
Campaign chapter selection now matches the new forest menus, with mission artwork, briefings, and a clear Begin Mission action.

Heroes now progress through 11 levels on a consistent combat-level XP curve. Neutral creeps can reach level 6; regular skills unlock ranks at 1/3/5 and ultimates at 5/8. Kill credit, allied sharing, AI learning, and save validation follow the same rules.
Map previews show one gold resource icon per nearby mine cluster instead of overlapping icons for every node.
Reworked the Marshal's spell visuals with amber leaf auras, a living chitin barrier, stronger Faultline impacts, and Crownfall's crown apparition and ground fractures.
Rally the Colony is now a persistent learned aura granting nearby allies 8/12/16% movement speed and 10/15/20% attack speed, with no mana cost or cooldown.
Terrain painting now displays imported ground atlases with automatic corner transitions and visual texture choices in the terrain panel.

Terrain editing now exposes cliff and bank edges, bank widths, and directional grid ramps. Failed edits retain their selection, while scenery placement, movement and deletion share terrain undo history and respect locks.

Echo Isles and Turtle Rock are now editable imported maps with difficulty-matched camps and usable starting areas. Local map saves support large terrain documents, and import reports show clearance adjustments.

Grid and imported-map water now use biome water profiles, with clearer shallow crossings, softer shoreline foam and distance-filtered caustics. Asset archival protects water profiles and ground materials used by saved maps.

Project maps now load their terrain only when opened or played, keeping large map documents out of the initial menu bundle. Map loading shows progress and safely handles cancellation or changing selections.
Warcraft imports now resolve ground materials around cliffs from the source cliff definitions, preserving those surfaces as editable texture layers. Echo Isles and Turtle Rock have been refreshed.
Terrain rendering uses less texture memory by sharing identical image channels and skipping unpainted materials, while preserving independently editable ground layers.

The editor now has a Decals toolbar tool with visible previews, Apply and Discard. Apply commits the whole batch in one undo step, previews stay out of saved maps, and decal positions support larger maps. MCP exposes the same preview workflow.
Water now blends calm, clear shallows into animated deep-water swells, with stylized foam and editable wave controls in water profiles.
Forest water is calmer, with less crest foam and irregular swells that break up repeating wave rows.
Forest water uses a darker, more muted blue-green tint while keeping shallow beds visible.
Forest shoreline foam is now barely visible; its water-profile control remains available for stronger foam later.
Skirmish and campaign matches now share the map editor’s Performance window, with live graphs, captures, draw-call inspection and organized match debug controls.
Shallow forest water has more visible gentle motion. The RTS camera starts at distance 60 and zooms between 40 and 80.
Reorganized the match HUD with top hero shortcuts, resources above the command grid, and FPS/zoom inside Debug beside Menu. The top Exit button is removed.
Units see downhill and across small hills within their vision radius, with a 2-metre uphill allowance while higher plateaus and solid bridge floors remain concealed.
Control group buttons appear only while populated, show their member count, and use a semi-transparent appearance.
Bound control groups keep fixed numbered positions, leaving empty space for unbound slots.
Control-group counts are larger with dark gray borders. The sun-and-moon display is hidden for now; the day/night cycle remains active.
Halls now show assigned Amber workers versus nearby mining capacity. Colonies begin with five workers in one row, automatically distributed across nearby deposits.
Amber sites now use five distinct crystal models, with shared one-third-remaining and empty appearances. The sun and moon HUD indicator is temporarily hidden.
New Queensguard Hall and Carapace Bastion models bring distinct ant and beetle materials, detailed textures, square building footprints, and player-colored roof and armor panels.
Forest lighting now uses neutral daylight and a cooler night look, with brief transitions and continuously moving shadows.
Starting workers face their nearby amber deposit and begin harvesting, with the hero on the opposite side of the hall, for both races.
Map editor Save now writes a map file explicitly. Automatic drafts and browser-library copies are removed, and mission tests use temporary previews.
Woodland trees now use richer painted foliage with diffuse lighting and shadows, without the white specular sheen that washed out their colours.
Resource counters now sit in one woodland ribbon with transparent amber, wood, root, and supply icons instead of separate framed tiles.
Woodland trees now have broader painted branch tiers, clearer trunks and roots, and lower mesh costs while preserving harvesting animations.
Balanced daylight and readable cool nights across painted terrain, foliage and buildings; original Warcraft terrain colors no longer receive a darkening multiplier.
Imported terrain now uses the installed Warcraft Definitive Edition textures and matching material maps, with native source resolutions preserved and clean texture transitions.
Choose and remember an explicit game render resolution, with a Native option and full-resolution interface text.
Woodland trees now have ragged painted foliage, brighter crowns, darker lower branches, and more substantial trunks.
Ant and beetle buildings now rise inside race-specific scaffolds with construction dust, then reveal their full model near completion.
Ant Barracks now use the red-leaf garrison design, and Beetle War Lodges have a new iron-and-shell model with player-colored armor panels.
Ant Chitin Works and Beetle Shell Forges now have distinct, player-colored workshop models.
Ant Houses and Beetle Brood Dens now use distinct leaf-and-silk and armored-shell supply models.
Ant workers now use the new Colony Worker model, with leaf team colors, a fitted resource backpack, and refined work and carrying animations.
Rally routes now start at building centers. Construction scaffolds rise from below ground without stretching, with larger, denser dust effects.
Ant Warriors now wear broad leaf helmets and shoulder armor for clearer team ownership, with the new cleaver model and a refined strike animation.
Player colors are brighter and easier to distinguish, with vivid red, blue and green armor and cleaner white team markings.
Construction dust is more abundant and scatters across scaffold roofs, sides and edges with varied timing instead of following a perimeter sequence.
Ant Archers now use the leaf-cloaked model with team colors, a refined running pose, and an animated bowstring and arrow release.
Weapon arrows, thorns and stones now use editable model effects shared with Spell & Effect Studio, with batched army volleys and validated publication limits.

Thornblades now fight with quick alternating dagger strikes and close gaps with a dedicated rapid lunge, an ivory trail, and subtle takeoff and contact dust. Charge effects remain editable in the Spell Editor.
Bombardier now uses its new back-mounted mortar model with braced recoil, arcing seed bombs and editable resin explosions. It is also recruitable from ant barracks after the Great Acorn Hall upgrade.

The Ant Marshal now uses a distinct animated hero model at twice the Warrior's scale, with matching selection size and formation spacing. The mixed-army preview includes learned Marshal spell controls.
Spell animations now use each model clip's authored impact timing consistently in the game and Spell Editor.
Rootbreaker's two-handed strikes have cleaner wrist deformation, and Uproot's club now meets the ground as the roots erupt.
Rootbreaker's model is 20% smaller while retaining his large collision radius and formation spacing.
Rootbreaker now runs with a nearly upright posture.

Reduced skirmish AI stalls from impossible retreat searches, removed unused aura visibility work, and prepared active unit navigation during loading to avoid first-order hitches. Added finer AI navigation timings for performance diagnosis.

Forest, foliage and decal generators preview their changes before Apply. Area cleanup removes selected scenery categories in bulk, respects locks and supports Undo, so generated placements can be edited individually afterward.
fixed: Building placement now checks units’ full collision bodies, preventing foundations from overlapping units whose centers are just outside the footprint.
Saves now retain combat pursuit of buildings positioned between navigation cells.
Calibrated building and resource model sizes to their grid footprints, kept depleted amber previews at the same scale, and reject starting bodies clipping adjacent obstacles.
Top-down editor zoom retains the current map dimensions when switching camera modes, allowing full overviews of larger maps.
Units can replan safely beside newly blocked terrain without snapping or getting stranded by grid rounding.
Movement planning no longer reveals unseen units through destination adjustments; physical collisions still apply.
Idle allies step aside to let crowded formations finish moving, while Hold Position and busy units remain protected.
Archers can enter rotated watchtowers with full body clearance, and occupied lookouts restore correctly from saves.
Hall upgrades preserve navigation caches, avoiding a full forest rebuild when the next tree is harvested.
Melee reinforcements find clear attack positions around allies, and crowded arrivals stay near the commanded destination instead of drifting away.
Map validation now rejects overlapping unit bodies across neighboring cells while respecting bridge levels and air units.

Aligned the game camera north-up with a steeper Warcraft-style view. The minimap now shows a horizontal camera outline, and viewport bounds prevent looking past map edges when panning, zooming or resizing.
Large units can cross bridge entrances with their full body footprint without getting stuck on the ramp.
HUD portraits now use a unit's map-authored appearance, matching its model on the battlefield.
Spell Studio now resolves preview-clone model scales correctly, so grouped targets and the caster remain visible while inspecting effects.
Saved games now accept moving-unit positions on large maps instead of retaining the old 512-cell coordinate limit.

Large imported maps now recover after editor reloads without the session-storage size limit. Recovery failures are visible, MCP supports direct map-file export/load, and importing detaches the previous file so Save cannot overwrite it.
Empty terrain no longer enables rock displacement, and erasing the final rock patch preserves loaded ground textures for undo.
Edits made while a map save is in progress remain marked unsaved instead of being incorrectly reported as saved.
Grid terrain selections now reach their exact height or water depth, with banks outside the selection. Adjacent regions join without ridges, and repeated edits preserve concave shorelines.

Editor startup, rendering, AI and navigation now consistently use committed terrain cells. Maps missing terrain or containing mismatched terrain dimensions are rejected instead of loading with fallback ground.

Terrain edits and map files now enforce valid height, water-depth and paint-coverage ranges. Invalid generator results cannot be applied, and Warcraft imports can use the full supported elevation span without clipping.
Repainting terrain now removes fully erased texture layers while preserving partially painted areas and Undo, avoiding unused material layers in saved maps and rendering.
MCP cleanup now uses its requested area and filters independently of unfinished editor selections, supports all cleanup categories and previews, and shares the editor's lock protection and Undo.
Terrain material settings now use a GPU lookup table, avoiding shader uniform limits when maps use many ground textures.
Applying forest and foliage previews no longer bakes their ground tint into permanent grass. Cleaning or moving vegetation removes its old tint while preserving painted grass and meadow terrain.
Fixed missing terrain textures in skirmish when fog of war exceeded the GPU texture limit. Editor and gameplay now share the corrected terrain shader.
Prewarm portrait and selection shaders during loading to reduce first-use match stutter.
Load amber depletion models before play so mining does not compile their shaders on first use.
Aligned Amber deposits into compact five-node mining lines beside the starting halls on Echo Isles and Turtle Rock, with clear worker approaches.
Buildings can now be placed on gently uneven ground; shared placement rules still reject sharp ledges, substantial slopes, water and blocked sites.
Fixed repeated early-match freezes caused by AI and units retrying unreachable paths.
Imported Warcraft terrain now uses a consistent installed Classic texture set, preserving painted shading without mod-pack mixing, warm overlays, or artificial specular sheen.
Warcraft map imports now remove hostile creeps around occupied starts before creating camps, matching the source game’s melee setup.
Warcraft imports now scale terrain and scenery to our five-cell halls, preserve atlas tiles at the matching scale, and keep starting mineral lines aligned with clear worker access.
Base worker-count labels stay crisp and consistently sized at every camera zoom and game render resolution.
Turtle Rock now uses the corrected battlefield scale, with properly spaced starting bases and five-node amber lines.
Ground units can see and target nearby flying enemies; flight altitude no longer incorrectly hides them as high-ground terrain.
Resizing model textures preserves neutral colors beneath team ownership masks instead of turning those surfaces black.
Flying units now fall onto the ground, water or deck beneath them during their death animation.
Hero skill learning now shows all four abilities in slots 1–4 without overlapping Back or hiding locked skills on another page.
Spell orders now move units into cast range before firing, following moving targets without spending mana or starting cooldowns early.
knownIssues: The expanded Beetle army art and remaining Ant units are still in development; Beetle units currently use placeholder models. Trailwarden and Broodseer are not part of the completed roster.

fixed: Desktop builds find the standard Rust installation when Cargo is missing from the shell PATH.
Generated spell icons now use the game's supported size, preventing startup failures.
